Current state:
- Latest head implements the algorithm (not just occlusion foundation): 17 coverage-engine files, worker, UI, tests. Joint mode genuinely evaluates candidate pairs by bitset union with quality/contribution tie-breakers, not greedy first-origin selection.
- Reviewer verdict: algorithm architecture 8/10, search-mode correctness 7.5/10, readiness for complex imported sets 4/10. Promising but not production-ready to merge.
- Recent follow-up work completed: aligned runtime shader to optimizer quality model (angle + texel density, winner-takes-most via pow(4), dominant-mode bias 1.15 for blend modes 2/3), removed stale distance-only blend constant/assertion, multiOriginInteraction.test.ts passes (36 tests), full unit suite passes (42 files, 371 tests), lint passes (tsc --noEmit), build passes (vite).

Key blockers from review (still open):
1. Imported sets can produce zero legal candidates. Extractor stores entire object AABB as obstacle; candidate clearance is distance from origin to AABB, so any origin inside the AABB gets zero clearance and is rejected. Affects single-GLB rooms, combined room+furniture, concave geometry, L-shaped walls, any large model whose AABB contains empty navigable space.
   Fix: use actual geometry clearance (camera sphere/capsule vs nearby triangles) via coverage BVH point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast. At minimum, obstacle bounds should be per connected mesh/spatial cluster, not per imported set object. Add regression test with one imported object containing floor, walls, empty interior.
2. Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports. Every triangle expanded into three independent Vec3 arrays + normal array + IDs + area; for 3M triangles minimum packed data ~144MB, actual JS objects/arrays/64-bit numbers several times larger, then structured-cloned into worker via postMessage creating another enormous representation. BVH recursively sorts/slices JS index arrays. Triangle intersection allocates temporary 3-element arrays, causing extreme GC pressure on millions of raycasts. Likely freezes/memory spikes/crashes on multi-million-triangle imports.
   Fix: compact typed arrays (positions Float32Array, indices Uint32Array, normals? Float32Array, meshRanges Uint32Array, transforms Float32Array), transfer ArrayBuffers into worker instead of cloning nested objects. For BVH: use three-mesh-bvh, flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, or per-mesh BVHs from existing indexed geometries. Avoid expanding indexed vertices into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle.
3. Geometry extraction still blocks main thread. Panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before creating/posting to worker, so worker only offloads optimizer, not scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, structured cloning. Complex model can freeze before worker reports first progress.
   Fix: move extraction into worker, or chunk it and yield between meshes.
4. "Apply to selected panorama pair" is conceptually wrong. UI writes optimized origins directly into existing panorama references via updatePanoReference(..., {origin: originA/B}). Existing panorama was rendered/captured from its original origin; changing metadata does not transform the image, just projects old pixels from wrong point, ruining alignment.
   Correct workflow: fixed-first — preserve existing panorama+origin, move next capture origin to B, render new graybox panorama, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary, associate with actual origin. Joint — create two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, associate each result with its actual origin. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Reachable upper bound mathematically inconsistent. reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank + all coarse candidates; final combined coverage uses different fine sample bank generated with seed+1. Same result shows both percentages and computes reachable efficiency, so UI can show Combined 83%, Reachable upper bound 80%, Reachable captured 100%. Clamp hides impossible ratio but doesn't repair incompatible estimates. Also fixed-first reachable set calculated before arbitrary first origin evaluated, so fixed first origin not included in reachable upper bound at all.
   Fix: use common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, efficiency. For fixed-first, include fixed origin in reachable union. Can still use separate coarse/fine search banks internally, but reported metrics must be evaluated on one shared final bank.
6. Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation. Joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation; fixed-first rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so identical candidate position can survive. Add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation.
7. Local candidates can float between floors. Candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below candidate; local offsets retain original Y. On sloped terrain/multilevel sets, offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor camera height, leaving origin floating meters above new floor.
   Fix: for each offset, find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance.
8. Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules. Optimizer evaluates angle and texel density; when both panoramas visible, actual shader still blends only by distance. Optimizer may prefer source for frontal angle while runtime favors closer but more grazing source; optimized coverage result and visible result don't fully agree. Shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging. (Partially addressed by recent shader alignment patch.)

Important refinements (not blockers but noted):
- "Four-level refinement" is not truly iterative. For every seed, all offsets generated around original seed (seed ± spacing/2, ±spacing/4, ±spacing/8, ±spacing/16). System does not select best half-step result and center quarter-step search around that new result. Still useful multiresolution neighborhood sample, but not the coordinate/pattern refinement described in plan. True refinement loop would update center after every level.
- Optimizer vs runtime quality mismatch noted above.

Testing assessment:
- Current tests are good unit tests but most dangerous cases absent: (1) one large imported object containing entire room; (2) 100k+ triangle performance fixture; (3) reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant; (4) fixed-first candidate separation; (5) sloped and multilevel floors; (6) existing panorama origins remaining immutable; (7) candidate generation inside concave imported geometry.
- No GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to latest head, so reported test suite not independently enforced in CI.
- Note: projectionCoverage.test.ts exists and runs both complete optimizer modes on a 100k+ triangle indexed fixture (39235ms), but reviewer still wants a full 100k+ optimizer integration test and a real complex imported-set benchmark.

User directive (sequence 762):
- Rebase onto main and resolve PR conflict.
- Add allowed-floor-region mechanism, or at least robust imported-floor component filtering.
- Run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add full 100K+ optimizer integration test, not merely BVH-construction test.
- Set a goal to accomplish the above; when work complete, spawn a subagent whose job is to disprove that the goal is actually fully complete. Have it report back what still is lacking. Then fix that, and repeat until subagent unable to find any holes.
